newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy's Padoa Schioppa named Consob head.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy's Padoa Schioppa named Consob head.

text.p: The Italian cabinet on Friday nominated vice director general of the Bank of Italy Tommaso Padoa Schioppa as the new chairman of stock market regulator Consob, a spokesman from the prime minister's office said.
Padoa Schioppa replaces Enzo Berlanda, whose mandate expires on Friday after five years in the post.
The cabinet also nominated Lamberto Cardia and Renato Rordorf as members of the stock market commission.
Rordorf is a magistrate at Italy's highest appeals court the Supreme Court.

Padoa Schioppa, 56, joined the Italian central bank originally in 1968, then in 1979 became director general for economic and financial affairs at the European Commission in Brussels before returning to the Bank of Italy as central director of economic research in 1983.

He became vice director general in 1984, was joint secretary of the Delors Committee on studying European economic and monetary union in the late 1980s and has held chairmanships of European Union banking committees and working groups.

He currently heads the Basle-based Bank for International Settlements banking supervisory committee and is a deputy member of the council of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the proposed European Central Bank.
